original_question: Let Omega be a connected open subset of R^n with n >= 2. Let A = A(x) be a symmetric matrix-valued coefficient field such that the elliptic equation div(A grad u) = 0 in Omega satisfies the uniform ellipticity bounds K^(-1)|xi|^2 <= A(x)xi·xi <= K|xi|^2 for all x, xi in R^n and the Lipschitz bound |A(x) - A(y)| <= E|x - y| for all x, y in R^n. Let u and v be two nonconstant solutions of div(A grad w) = 0 in Omega, let S be a connected smooth hypersurface of dimension n-1 contained in Omega, and let Sigma be an open proper subset of S. If u = 0 on all of S and v = 0 on Sigma, must v also vanish on all of S?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.1, "Unique continuation along level surfaces," in Section 3 of the paper. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official problem extremely closely: it has the same divergence-form elliptic equation, the same symmetry, uniform ellipticity, and Lipschitz hypotheses on A, the same connected open set Omega subset R^n with n >= 2, the same data of two nonconstant solutions u and v, the same connected smooth (n-1)-dimensional hypersurface S and open proper subset Sigma subset S, and the same conclusion being asked, namely whether v must vanish on all of S. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
missing_details: The paper states only that u and v are "solutions" of div(A grad w)=0; to make the question fully stand-alone, it is better to say explicitly that they are real-valued weak solutions, for example in H^1_loc(Omega). ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))

Because Sigma is a subset of the hypersurface S, "open proper subset" should be understood in the relative topology of S. The paper leaves this implicit. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))

To make the coefficient assumptions fully explicit, it helps to state that A is a real symmetric matrix field with values in R^{n x n}_sym and that K,E are positive constants appearing in the ellipticity and Lipschitz bounds. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
refined_question: Let Omega subset R^n, with n >= 2, be a connected open set, and let A: R^n -> R^{n x n}_sym be a real symmetric matrix field such that, for some constants K,E > 0, one has K^{-1}|xi|^2 <= A(x)xi·xi <= K|xi|^2 for all x,xi in R^n and |A(x)-A(y)| <= E|x-y| for all x,y in R^n. If u,v in H^1_loc(Omega) are nonconstant real-valued weak solutions of div(A grad w)=0 in Omega, if S subset Omega is a connected smooth hypersurface of dimension n-1, and if Sigma is a relatively open proper subset of S such that u = 0 on S and v = 0 on Sigma, must it follow that v = 0 on all of S? ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the paper's less standard unique-continuation problem along a level surface of another solution. The surrounding context introduces this question after fixing the divergence-form elliptic equation and the ellipticity/Lipschitz assumptions precisely so that the standard unique continuation property is available; the paper then asks for the stronger propagation-of-vanishing statement along a connected smooth hypersurface contained in the zero set of u. The nearby discussion also explains the intended scope: the problem arose from inverse problems for cracks in inhomogeneous media, the answer is affirmative when A = I because S is then analytic, and some smoothness of S is genuinely necessary, as shown by the planar harmonic counterexample with a corner. So the right refinement is to keep the question exactly in this linear elliptic, smooth-hypersurface setting and only make implicit conventions explicit. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
